corpus_maintenance: Served frontend assets (status 200, raw-body, text/html|javascript|css) are NOT body-asserted. Their records carry body_assertion instead of body_sha256/body_bytes/body_text, and a record with no body_sha256 is not body-asserted by the replay. Pinning an asset's bytes is not a product assertion -- it reddens on every deliberate frontend edit and says nothing about what changed -- and with no recorder left the only repair was hand-patching a hash. Status, content type, content disposition and Location are still asserted for these routes, and API response bodies (normalized-json) are still fully asserted. Assert frontend CONTENT with a targeted check on the thing you care about, never a whole-file digest.

coverage_limits.a_green_replay_does_not_prove: mutation semantics. Write probes here are overwhelmingly REFUSALS: 280 cases use a mutating method but only 6 returned 2xx and therefore actually changed state. A route's refusal envelope being pinned says nothing about what a SUCCESSFUL call does, and nothing at all about what a successful SECOND call does.
coverage_limits.read_the_producer: For any handler this corpus does not exercise on its success path, the oracle is the reference source, not this file. Helpers named generate/ensure/init/create/set may be fill-only-when-absent; read the guard before porting, and assert BOTH directions.

native_deviations.native: 400 missing_request_body, the same typed refusal every other write route on this surface already answers
native_deviations.reference: 500 settings_operation_failed -- the handler calls request.get_json() without silent=True, werkzeug raises UnsupportedMediaType, and the route's blanket except turns an unhandled exception into a generic failure
native_deviations.why: a raise is not a refusal. Every sibling route on this surface answers missing_request_body for the identical input, and the reference's own generator comments approve of that answer; reproducing the 500 would be preserving a defect, not fidelity.

native_deviations.native: the session gate's own answer -- 302 to /init when unestablished, 500 in the owner's voice when corrupt -- and the 308 in the six established phases
native_deviations.reference: 308 to /app/thinking/ in EVERY phase -- Werkzeug raises the strict-slash redirect during URL matching, which is before before_request, so the session gate never sees it
native_deviations.when: the journal is unestablished or its config is corrupt
native_deviations.why: the redirect is a route in the native shell, so it sits INSIDE the session-gate layer rather than ahead of it. Matching the reference here would mean widening a shared, closed session-gate exemption inventory for a redirect, and the owner-visible result is better without it: someone who has not set up a journal is sent to setup rather than to a page that will immediately send them to setup. ⚠ This is a FRAMEWORK difference, not a narrowed contract -- the 308 itself is reproduced wherever the gate admits the request.

native_deviations.native: local_runtime.status is blocked when the readable runtime phase is stopped
native_deviations.reference: local_runtime.status is ok next to the stopped phase
native_deviations.when: an established projection has no running local runtime
native_deviations.why: runtime status now reports whether thinking can run, not merely whether the health record was readable. A stopped runtime cannot honestly report ok.
